newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan downgrading status of Japan envoys - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan downgrading status of Japan envoys - paper.

text.p: Taipei will cancel some privileges enjoyed by Japan's de facto diplomats in Taiwan to reciprocate for Japan's refusal to upgrade treatment of Taiwan's unofficial representatives there, a local newspaper said on Wednesday.

The planned reprisals, if carried out, would likely deepen a growing rift between Taiwan and Japan over disputed islands. The Central Daily News said Japan's representatives in Taiwan would be stripped of tax exemptions and their car registrations would be downgraded to those of foreign organisations rather than diplomats.
Taiwan's Foreign Ministry made the decision after Japan rebuffed Taipei's request to upgrade the status of its representatives in Tokyo, the report said.
Japan has no diplomatic ties with Taiwan's Republic of China government, but they share close economic, social and cultural ties managed by offices that are embassies in everything but name.
Foreign Ministry officials declined comment on the report.
Taipei and Tokyo are locked in a sovereignty dispute over ownership of an uninhabited East China Sea archipelago and fishing rights in waters around the islands.

Japan's assertion of sovereignty of the islands and its use of patrol ships to keep Taiwanese vessels at bay have fuelled anti-Japanese sentiment in Taiwan as well as in Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China.
Since 1972, Tokyo has recognised the communist government in Beijing, Taiwan's arch rival since the Chinese civil war split them in 1949, as the only government of China.
